reference.source: GeneReviews / Bradley's Neurology in Clinical Practice
clinicalPearls: SPG7, caused by biallelic SPG7 variants encoding the mitochondrial protein paraplegin, is usually recessive and frequently presents as a complicated HSP
A mixed spastic-ataxic phenotype is characteristic, with cerebellar signs (nystagmus, dysarthria, limb ataxia) accompanying the lower-limb spasticity
Optic atrophy and progressive external ophthalmoplegia may occur, reflecting the mitochondrial basis of the disorder
Onset is typically in adulthood, and SPG7 is one of the more common identifiable causes of otherwise unexplained adult spastic ataxia
MRI often shows cerebellar atrophy in addition to changes of corticospinal degeneration
Some heterozygous carriers may show subtle features, and SPG7 should be considered in apparently sporadic adult-onset cases
Management is symptomatic, addressing spasticity, ataxia, bladder dysfunction, and any ophthalmological complications
reference.pathophysiology: Hereditary spastic paraplegias arise from length-dependent degeneration of the longest corticospinal (and often dorsal-column) axons. SPG7 encodes paraplegin, a subunit of the m-AAA protease complex located in the inner mitochondrial membrane, which is responsible for quality control and processing of mitochondrial proteins. Loss of functional paraplegin impairs mitochondrial proteostasis and oxidative phosphorylation, and the high energy demand of long axons and Purkinje neurones renders them selectively vulnerable, producing the combined corticospinal and cerebellar degeneration seen clinically.
additionalDifferentials: Other hereditary spastic paraplegias (e.g. SPG4, SPG11)
Autosomal recessive cerebellar ataxias, including Friedreich ataxia
Mitochondrial disorders with spasticity and ophthalmoplegia
Multiple sclerosis presenting with spastic ataxia
additionalInvestigations: MRI of the brain and spine to assess cerebellar atrophy and exclude structural mimics
Genetic testing for SPG7, including deletion/duplication analysis, within an HSP/ataxia panel
Ophthalmological assessment for optic atrophy and external ophthalmoplegia
Serum lactate and consideration of mitochondrial workup where systemic features are present
Nerve conduction studies to characterise any associated neuropathy
redFlags: Prominent ophthalmoplegia, ptosis, or systemic features suggesting a broader mitochondrial disorder needing evaluation
Rapidly progressive ataxia or new brainstem signs prompting reassessment for alternative causes
Visual loss from optic atrophy requiring ophthalmological input
New myelopathic signs or a sensory level indicating a compressive lesion
reference.prognosis: SPG7 is slowly progressive; combined spasticity and ataxia lead to gradually increasing gait disability over years to decades, though many patients remain ambulant with aids and overall life expectancy is usually preserved.
pitfalls: Dismissing SPG7 in apparently sporadic adult-onset spastic ataxia because of an absent family history
Failing to recognise the cerebellar and optic features as part of a single complicated HSP phenotype
Overlooking mitochondrial comorbidity when ophthalmoplegia is present
Attributing the presentation solely to multiple sclerosis without genetic evaluation
management: No disease-specific therapy exists; control lower-limb spasticity with oral antispasticity agents such as baclofen or tizanidine, focal botulinum toxin injection for troublesome muscle groups, and intrathecal baclofen in refractory cases
Regular physiotherapy with stretching, gait training, ankle-foot orthoses and walking aids to preserve mobility and prevent contractures
Address the cerebellar component with balance and coordination rehabilitation, and refer for ophthalmology assessment and low-vision support for optic atrophy and external ophthalmoplegia
Manage neurogenic bladder symptoms with antimuscarinic agents and continence support, and treat neuropathic pain and fatigue symptomatically
Periodic surveillance for progression, falls risk, swallowing and bladder dysfunction to guide escalation of aids and interventions
Multidisciplinary care coordinated between neurology, clinical genetics, physiotherapy, occupational therapy and orthotics
Offer genetic counselling and family testing, noting the usually autosomal recessive inheritance of biallelic SPG7 variants
